run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T01:20:05Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by a Chaos Mesh network fault. Events record a Schedule in namespace chaos-mesh named otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition that spawned one NetworkChaos object per minute from 01:19:59Z to 01:28:59Z; each object reported 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/shipping-75d58f5d84-jgxvv' and 'otel-demo/quote-6b5877698d-8fn9w' and recovered about 55s later. frontend-proxy error span rate was 0 at 00:57:05, at most 0.019/s through 01:19:05, then 0.078/s at 01:21:05, 0.526/s at 01:23:05 and 0.889-0.967/s through 01:33:05. The failing spans are frontend-proxy 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress' with http.status_code=500, propagated from frontend 'POST /api/checkout' -> checkout 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' (rpc.grpc.status_code=13, 'shipping quote failure: failed POST to email service: expected 200, got 500') -> shipping '/get-quote' ('Internal Server Error') -> shipping 'POST quote' which lasts ~5.00s and ends 'Timeout'. Shipping's only configured HTTP dependency on that path is QUOTE_ADDR=http://quote:8080, shipping logs show continuous 'Requesting quote' with 'Sending Quote' only in bursts at 01:28:54 and 01:29:54, and a sampled trace at 01:28:54 shows the same shipping->quote->email path completing in milliseconds with email returning http.status_code=200. All 21 otel-demo pods were Running with 0 restarts, all flagd fault flags are 'off', and email's own spans stayed fast and successful, so pod crashes, flagd injection and an email-service failure are not supported as causes. Remaining uncertainty: the NetworkChaos and Schedule specs cannot be read with the available tools, events stop at 01:28:59 while errors stay elevated to about 01:33, and the trace message names the email service although the configured POST target on that path is the quote service.

claims.text: frontend-proxy 5m span error rate was 0 at 00:57:05, at most 0.019/s from 00:59:05 to 01:19:05, then 0.078/s at 01:21:05, 0.526/s at 01:23:05, and 0.889-0.967/s from 01:25:05 to 01:33:05; the series' last point at 01:37:05 was 0.
frontend-proxy's own error spans during the incident belong to the operations 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress', both with error=true and http.status_code=500.

Error-status span rate by service rose together for checkout (~0.87-0.96/s), frontend (~1.69-1.94/s), frontend-proxy (~0.89-0.97/s) and shipping (~0.89-0.96/s) from 01:23:05 to 01:33:05; accounting and payment were 0 across the series, and ad, fraud-detection and recommendation showed only sparse 0.0037/s points that also occurred before 01:19.

The failing operations in the 10m increase of error spans are shipping 'POST quote' and '/get-quote', checkout 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' and 'HTTP POST', frontend 'POST /api/checkout', 'POST', 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' and 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder', and frontend-proxy 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress'.

A full trace (27fd79ac35376775a1967f931893f9ab) shows this parent-child chain from visible parent references: frontend-proxy 'ingress' (5.009686s, HTTP 500) -> frontend-proxy 'router frontend egress' (5.009616s, 500) -> frontend 'POST /api/checkout' (5.009120s, 500) -> checkout 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' (5.006153s, rpc.grpc.status_code=13, 'shipping quote failure: failed POST to email service: expected 200, got 500') -> checkout 'HTTP POST' (5.002741s) -> shipping '/get-quote' (5.001391s, 'Internal Server Error') -> shipping 'POST quote' (5.001336s, 'Timeout').

The shipping Deployment's only configured HTTP dependency on this path is QUOTE_ADDR=http://quote:8080, and Kubernetes wiring is consistent: Service 'quote' selects opentelemetry.io/name=quote with endpoint 100.96.1.165 (pod quote-6b5877698d-8fn9w) and Service 'email' selects opentelemetry.io/name=email with endpoint 100.96.2.193 (pod email-59f69bc6cf-8z5c5).

The quote service's span rate for 'POST /getquote', 'calculate-quote' and '{closure}' fell from about 0.56/s at 01:17:05 to about 0.09/s from 01:25:05 onward, and all of its spans carry STATUS_CODE_UNSET rather than an error status.

The email service's span rate for 'POST /send_order_confirmation', 'send_email' and 'sinatra.render_template' fell the same way (about 0.55/s to about 0.09/s) over the same interval, with no error status recorded on its spans.
In the newest 60 matching shipping log lines read, 'Requesting quote' appears continuously through the incident while 'Sending Quote' appears only in bursts around 01:28:54 and 01:29:54.

A sampled healthy checkout trace at 01:28:54 shows shipping '/get-quote' at 1588us, shipping 'POST quote' at 1486us, quote 'POST /getquote' at 318us, and email 'POST /send_order_confirmation' with http.status_code=200 in 5167us — the same path completing normally.
Email's p99 span duration for 'POST /send_order_confirmation' stayed between about 96ms and 352ms from 00:57 to 01:35, showing no multi-second degradation of its own.

Events record involvedObject.kind=Schedule, namespace=chaos-mesh, name=otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition with reason=Spawned and message 'Create new object: otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition-<suffix>' once per minute from 01:19:59Z through 01:28:59Z (suffixes 9xnx8, nz4lm, 85v74, rw58g, lwvxl, 769cj, q7g8w, fsflv, 5ks6l, 5czjs).

Events for those NetworkChaos objects record reason=Applied with messages 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/shipping-75d58f5d84-jgxvv' and 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/quote-6b5877698d-8fn9w', followed each minute by 'Time up according to the duration' (TimeUp) and 'Successfully recover chaos for ...' at :54, with PodNetworkChaos Updated events on the same two pods; window-wide grouping counts 20 NetworkChaos Applied, 18 Recovered, 9 TimeUp and 38 PodNetworkChaos Updated events in otel-demo.

The frontend-proxy 'ingress' error rate at 3-minute resolution was 0.0067/s at 01:20:00, 0.067/s at 01:21:00, 0.24/s at 01:22:00 and 0.41-0.48/s from 01:23:00 to 01:33:00, while the first Schedule Spawned event is at 01:19:59.

All 21 pods in namespace otel-demo were Running with restartCount 0 and start times around 00:43:16-00:45:05, and the email, frontend-proxy, quote and shipping Deployments each reported replicas=1, ready=1, available=1.

Every fault-injection flag in the otel-demo flagd-config ConfigMap (adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure) has defaultVariant 'off'.

Most likely mechanism: the NetworkChaos objects spawned by Schedule otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition severed traffic between the shipping pod and the quote pod, so shipping's POST to quote:8080 hung to its ~5s client timeout (span error 'Timeout'), shipping's /get-quote returned 500, and the failure propagated checkout -> frontend -> frontend-proxy 'ingress', where RequestErrorRate fired. Corroboration: chaos applied and recovered on exactly those two pods each minute, shipping quote successes only at the :54 recovery instants, 5.00s 'POST quote' spans, and a normal millisecond shipping->quote call in the 01:28:54 trace.

The exact text 'failed POST to email service: expected 200, got 500' names the email service, but no email failure is observed; the POST configured on this code path targets quote (QUOTE_ADDR=http://quote:8080) and email answered 200 in a healthy trace, so the hypothesis is that the message's service label does not identify the endpoint actually targeted. The message's origin could not be verified without image or source access.

An email-service failure of its own is not supported: email spans returned http.status_code=200 during the incident-shaped window (01:28:54) and its p99 latency stayed at 96-352ms; email's traffic collapse to about 0.09/s matches quote's collapse, consistent with fewer orders completing rather than email erroring.

The window-wide event grouping contains no Pod reason such as OOMKilling, Evicted or BackOff for otel-demo; the Pod-level lifecycle reasons it lists (Created, Pulled, Scheduled, Started, SuccessfulAttachVolume, FailedScheduling, Killing) all belong to namespace data-recorders, which is unrelated to the otel-demo checkout path.

Pod crash, restart or resource-driven failure in otel-demo is rejected as the cause: all 21 otel-demo pods were Running with restartCount 0 and start times before the incident (~00:43), and the four workloads on the failing path were ready and available.

flagd-driven fault injection is rejected as the cause this window: every flag in the flagd-config ConfigMap has defaultVariant 'off', and no flag declares a shipping, quote or email request-failure injection.

Review and, if the experiment is not intentional, suspend the Chaos Mesh Schedule 'otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition' in namespace chaos-mesh and its spawned NetworkChaos objects; because those custom resources are not exposed by the available Kubernetes tools, inspect them with Chaos Mesh or kubectl tooling to confirm the selector, direction and target, since the events show the effect on pods shipping-75d58f5d84-jgxvv and quote-6b5877698d-8fn9w even though the object name says 'email-checkout'.

Locate the RequestErrorRate alerting rule in the Prometheus instance that feeds Alertmanager and confirm its expression, evaluation window and threshold, because a rule-name query against this target returned no rule named RequestErrorRate, so the reported value 0.6444 was not reproduced from rule state.

gaps: NetworkChaos and Schedule custom resources could not be read (kinds outside the available Kubernetes tool list), so the injected experiment's selector, direction, target, mode and duration are unverified; the mechanism is inferred from events plus telemetry.

Chaos events were captured only through 01:28:59Z (event source end 01:29:27Z) while frontend-proxy errors were still elevated in metric samples to about 01:33-01:35; spawns and recoveries after 01:28:59 are unknown.
The end of the error episode is not established: one 3-minute query's metric data ended at data_as_of 01:35:00, so 01:36 onward is unknown rather than proven recovered.
The alerting rule RequestErrorRate was not returned on this Prometheus: the list_prometheus_rules query returned nothing (status no_data), so the alert expression and threshold are unverified.

The email container produced no log lines for 01:15:00-01:37:31 (0 lines read, status no_data), so email's application-level behavior during failed orders is unverified beyond trace status and latency.

The origin of the error string 'failed POST to email service: expected 200, got 500' and its mismatch with the configured quote target could not be verified (no image contents or source available); why the experiment is named 'email-checkout' while applied to quote and shipping pods is also unknown.
Queries for NetworkPolicy and ResourceQuota objects in namespace otel-demo returned no objects (status no_data), so those candidate causes could not be assessed either way from citable evidence.
The 10-minute grpc client metric query for rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count returned no data (status no_data), so gRPC-level client error codes were only observed from trace span tags.
Customer or business impact beyond the demo load-generator's own 'POST' spans returning http.status_code=500 is not verified.
next_steps: Inspect the Chaos Mesh Schedule and NetworkChaos objects named otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition(-*) in namespace chaos-mesh with Chaos Mesh or kubectl tooling to confirm the exact partition spec.
Confirm whether the experiment is intentional; if not, suspend the Schedule and verify that frontend-proxy 'ingress' and shipping 'POST quote' error spans stop.
Check the Prometheus instance that evaluates RequestErrorRate to read its expression and confirm the reported error ratio of 0.6444 for otel-demo/frontend-proxy.
Review shipping's quote client timeout and error message text with the application owners so a quote-path failure is not reported as an email-service POST failure.
